requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
The two marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`, including the boundaries the text names.

**Stop when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first consecutive transient failure**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute]` feeds repeated 429 failures into `ProviderBackoff::retry` with a simulated clock. It asserts that every `Retry::Wait` leaves the next attempt no later than `start + 60s`. It also asserts that retries eventually end in `Retry::Stop`, after more than three attempts.
- It checks the boundary from the first failure. A second failure at `start + 58s` waits no more than 2s, so the delay is capped by the one-minute point.
- It covers `Retry-After` past the point, in three cases:
  - `Retry-After: 60` waits exactly 60s.
  - `Retry-After: 61` stops at once.
  - `Retry-After: 90` stops at once.
  
  This matches "including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point", and the exact-minute boundary is not off by one.
- A second path covers a first failure that does not stop. When the first failure is at `start + RETRY_LIMIT`, `retry` returns `Wait`. A later failure at `start + 3*RETRY_LIMIT` returns `Stop` with `io::ErrorKind::TimedOut`. This is checked for three failure kinds: 503, a Bedrock code only, and a timeout.
- A permanent 400 `ValidationException` stops with its own error, not the "kept failing" error. This confirms the limit error is only for transient failures.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_request_failing_for_a_minute_fails_the_assessment]` runs the whole `assess` flow under paused tokio time. The provider always returns 503 `ServiceUnavailableException`. It asserts that elapsed time is at most `RETRY_LIMIT`, that more than three requests were made, and that `assess` returns an error. It also checks the usage log, where the final attempt is recorded with `retried == false`.

**Fail with an error naming the attempt count and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available**
- The unit test asserts the message contains "kept failing for a minute", "after {attempts+1} attempts", and "HTTP 429 ThrottlingException".
- The integration test asserts the exact text "after {attempts} attempts; last failure: HTTP 503 ServiceUnavailableException". It takes `attempts` from the provider's recorded request count, so the number is the real attempt count.
- The "when available" cases are covered separately: status only (`HTTP 503`), code only (`ThrottlingException`), and neither (a timeout, with "no response within ten minutes").

I found no unaddressed obligation or boundary. The cited `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` behaviors (delay selection, resetting on success, and so on) belong to that requirement and are not assessed here.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
